ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 imposes a two-limb contact obligation before a driver may cancel for no-show: the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The platform's own trip record shows message_count 2 but in_app_calls as an empty array and call_count 0, and the derived contact_before_cancel block records obligation_met = false, with cancellation at 19:54:00 after the two messages at 19:48:00 and 19:51:30. The call limb therefore fails on the authoritative telemetry, and the fee must be voided: FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD charged, with no driver compensation.

The message limb cannot carry the obligation on its own. The chat log for this trip contains exactly two entries, both plain IN_APP text messages from the driver ('Reached Blk 106, at the drop off' at 19:48:00 and 'Waiting ah, pls come' at 19:51:30), and no voice-call entry of any kind. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive - it requires a message AND a call - so two messages with zero calls does not meet it, and the fee is voided.

The driver's counter-statement asserts 'I called her two times and messaged'. That assertion is not borne out by any artifact: the platform call ledger in the trip record is empty and the chat log carries no voice-call entry, only the two text messages quoted. The only record of a call anywhere in this case is the driver's own uncorroborated sentence, and POL-NS-23 is written against what the trip record and chat log show, not against what a party says after the fact. The rider's account - 'I never got any call from the driver, only two messages' - is the account the platform data matches, and it is the rider's account that is corroborated.

There is no open question here of the kind POL-GEN-26 exists for. Whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is the fact POL-NS-23 turns on, and it is established by two artifacts of uncontested weight: the trip record and the chat log, each graded COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0. The one missing artifact, EV-ADVIS-06053-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, status MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), carries no fact at all and concerns road-traffic conditions, which no clause in the no-show category uses; its absence cannot unsettle a contact-obligation finding, and no outcome should be withheld on account of it.

The rider does not contest that the driver reached the pickup point: the GPS arrival check is corroborated, the nearest fix sits 1.27 m from the pickup at 4 m reported accuracy, and the driver's fix then holds at 0 kph through the wait window. That concession does not help the driver. POL-NS-21's free wait and POL-NS-23's contact obligation are separate requirements, and a punctual arrival does not cure a failure to place the required in-app call; the fee still falls.

On the money: the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and refund_if_voided_sgd 5.00, so the rider is presently carrying the whole disputed charge. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION would leave that present state standing and the rider out of pocket; FULL_REFUND is the outcome the rider's claim supports, and the amount to move is the full 5.00 SGD, which matches the policy fee of 5.00 SGD so no fee-amount adjustment is in play.

This is a case the AI can finish. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; there is no safety flag on the dispute; and the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 0, so the 0.95 uplift is not engaged. POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final in these circumstances, so a monetary ruling - FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD fee - should issue rather than any escalation.

The driver was physically at the pickup and the arrival is corroborated: the arrival check on the GPS trace confirms the 19:47:40 arrival event, the nearest fix sitting 1.27 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4 m — far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — so the event from which POL-NS-21 starts the free wait is established on the record.

The free wait was served in full before the driver cancelled: the driver arrived at 19:47:40, the 300 s wait ran from that arrival and expired at 19:52:45, and the driver did not cancel until 19:54:00 — 380 s after arrival and 80 s past expiry. On POL-NS-21's terms this was a valid rider no-show cancellation; the record shows no early cancel and no short-cut.

The amount charged is exactly the policy figure, so there is no over-charge to correct: the payments ledger carries a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line that reconciles to the total, matching the 5.00 SGD fee POL-NS-22 fixes, and if the fee stands POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with 5.00 SGD to the driver.

The message limb of POL-NS-23 is satisfied and the rider had actual notice the driver was waiting: the driver sent two in-app messages before cancelling, at 19:48:00 and 19:51:30, and the chat log records the rider reading both, at 19:48:32 and 19:51:44, each before the 19:54:00 cancellation.

I do not press that POL-NS-23's second limb is met, because the record does not carry it: the trip record's in_app_calls is empty and the derived contact_before_cancel reports call_count 0 and obligation_met false, and the chat log contains no voice-call entry. The driver's on-file account asserts two calls, but the platform record — which the clause expressly relies on for this fact — carries none, so on the record as it stands the call limb fails.

ruling.explanation:
The rider filed this dispute, so the outcome is read from the rider's claim on the 5.00 SGD contested. The money at issue is clear on the payments ledger (EV-FARE-06053): a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total charged 5.00 SGD, refund issued 0.00 SGD.

Two requirements govern a no-show cancellation, and they are separate.

First, the free wait (POL-NS-21). The driver's arrival at 19:47:40 is corroborated by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-06053): the nearest fix sits 1.27 m from the pickup within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, at 4 m reported accuracy. The 300-second free wait ran from that arrival and expired at 19:52:45; the driver cancelled at 19:54:00, after expiry. The rider expressly does not contest this, and the driver's arrival and free-wait claims are accepted.

Second, the contact obligation (POL-NS-23). Before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before cancelled_at. The message limb is met: the chat log (EV-CHAT-06053) carries two driver messages, at 19:48:00 and 19:51:30, both read by the rider before the 19:54:00 cancellation. The call limb fails: trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty array, the derived contact_before_cancel block reports call_count 0 and obligation_met = false, and the chat log contains no voice-call entry. POL-NS-23 reads the trip record and the chat log as its own test. The driver's counter-statement asserting 'I called her two times' is uncorroborated by any artifact and does not stand in for that test, so it cannot make the limb hold. Because the call limb is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee and directs a full refund of the amount charged, with no driver compensation.

The driver's remaining points are answered. The fee charged exactly matches the 5.00 SGD policy figure, so there is no over-charge to correct and no fee-amount referral under POL-NS-22. But POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome follows only where the fee stands; here POL-NS-23 voids it, so no compensation is payable. The driver's own advocate does not press that the call limb is met.

There is no open question requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26. The facts POL-NS-23 turns on are carried by two COMPLETE artifacts of weight 1.0 (the trip record and the chat log), not by missing or impaired evidence. The one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-06053-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, weight 0.0), carries no fact and concerns road conditions, which no no-show clause uses. This is a dispute below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band with no fraud flag and no safety flag, so POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make this AI ruling final.

No referral is produced by any clause: no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit (the driver arrived, and did attempt contact by message), no POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag (the named field is absent and the fee does not stand), and no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral (the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD).

Result: the rider is refunded the full 5.00 SGD charged; the driver receives no compensation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
